The next steps are generic and omit the targeted recommendations in the rationale.","problems":["Headline and rationale say the excess 'sits mostly in multimorbid patients' and is 'concentrated where it would be expected', but the same text says the excess 'persists after risk adjustment' (5.79x expected, 5.37 score). The framing downplays a strong signal and is internally inconsistent.","Headline says the few charts 'support the billed levels', yet the sample is only 4 of 50 99215 claims, and the 'inconclusive' lean sits awkwardly with a z of 4.69 and 5.79x ratio.","Claim that 'even within each complexity tier the share runs several times the all-provider rate' is not true for every tier (e.g. 0-condition tier is 0.0 vs 0.022, 3 conditions 0.176 vs 0.074 is ~2.4x); overstated.","The 'against 14% for comparison providers' figure is stated, but with 0 of 4 documented it is a weak comparison; the rate difference is not meaningfully interpretable.","Cited claims C0071624 and C0071729 are low-complexity examples; the sentence on documentation cites C0071629 and C0071653 in the text but they are not in cited_claim_ids, and the structured citations omit them and C0071742.","Next steps are generic ('larger sample of 99214 and 99215 claims', 'Re-screen') and do not name specific claims, whereas the rationale recommends targeting low-complexity and 2-3 condition tiers and checking cloned MDM language; the actionable specifics are not in next_steps.","Rationale is long and includes a mechanically appended Examples section that repeats earlier content, with the 'quick chart pull' for 18-year-old being a minor point since it is only 1 of 3 low-complexity claims."]}
